Sophia: Heads-up — bringing up HF model `hf/xl-chat-v1` on Redwood dedicated; seeing a weird eval regression after quant + conversion.
Matt: What kind of regression? LL or generation quality?
Sophia: Perplexity jump on our convo evals and some hallucinations in instruction-following tests. Numbers: baseline fp16 ppl=12.1, converted+quant ppl=18.7.
Raj: oof. Any diffs in tokenization or chat template? Those bite us a lot.
Sophia: I ran a quick token diff — found that the HF tokenizer inserts a leading special token (\u201c<|start|>\u201d) and our conversion mapping dropped it; that shifts sliding_window offsets.
Lisa: That would misalign KV cache windows if sliding_window is applied based on token counts.
Matt: Show the config.json you used.
Sophia: Here — converted config snippet we used:
```json
"hidden_size": 4096,
"num_attention_heads": 32,
"num_key_value_heads": 8,
"max_position_embeddings": 2048,
"sliding_window": 512,
"rope_scaling": { "factor": 1.0 },
"special_tokens": { "bos_token": "<|start|>", "eos_token": "</s>" }
```
Raj: Two immediate red flags: 1) `num_key_value_heads` != `num_attention_heads` / head-share policy on this model, 2) `sliding_window` logic expects templates without an implied BOS.
Sophia: Yep. When I patched to explicitly map the HF special token to Redwood BOS and recomputed offsets, ppl dropped to ~13.4, still not baseline.
Lisa: Did you try rope scaling mismatch? Some HF-to-Redwood conversions assume default rope_scaling=none but HF model may have per-layer scaling baked in.
Matt: Also quantization can amplify tiny phase shifts from ROTARY/rope errors. Which quant bits?
Sophia: 4-bit GPTQ with per-channel scale. Re-ran with fp16 weights (no quant) and after fixing special token alignment ppl=12.4 — close to baseline. So quantization + misalignment = bad combo.
Raj: This suggests two-pronged fix: (A) ensure tokenizer->chat template mapping preserves or strips special tokens consistently; (B) verify `num_key_value_heads` mapping and enforce `rope_scaling` parity (or apply calibrated multiplier).
Lisa: For (A) we should add a converter check that computes token_count_difference = tokenized_with_hf - tokenized_with_redwood_template and fails the conversion if non-zero. Quick pseudo: `if diff != 0: warn_and_require_manual_review()`
Matt: We should also add an eval smoke test in the onboarding flow: run a short conv with known golden and compare logits/ppl within eps tolerance after conversion and after quant.
Sophia: I added a failing CI test locally. Repro command I used:
```bash
python tools/convert_hf.py --hf-model hf/xl-chat-v1 --out redwood-model/ --map-specials yes
python tests/onboard_smoke.py --model redwood-model/ --quant 4bit
```
Matt: Can you paste the token diff sample?
Sophia: Sure — tokenized outputs for prompt "Hello, how are you?":
HF: [50256, 401, 345, 318]  (leading 50256 = <|start|>)
Redwood (converted): [401, 345, 318]
-> sliding_window anchored at different positions leading to KV read offset by 1 token.
Raj: Add a conversion rule: if HF has a BOS id that is not part of chat_template, set `strip_bos=true` and adjust sliding_window accordingly. Also validate `max_position_embeddings` >= tokenized_length + reserved_specials.
Lisa: I'll open a quick PR with: 1) token-diff check, 2) KV-head consistency check, 3) rope_scaling parity assert.
Sophia: Thanks — I'll re-run quant experiments after PR lands. Adding an eval note: when quantized, tolerances should be looser for ppl but we should flag >20% degradation automatically.
deploy-bot: new-deploy/redwood-converter v0.27 deployed to staging :rocket:
Matt: Nice. Can someone add this case to the onboarding checklist and the model playbook? Put it under "Tokenization & positional checks".
Sophia: On it. I'll also collect a small corpus of failing prompts to track post-quant regressions. :memo:
Lisa: filing PR now — cc @Sophia @Matt @Raj :eyes:
Sophia: quick follow-up: do we want to try rope_rescale per-layer multiplier (0.997) like HF uses for this family? Could bridge the remaining ppl gap without touching quant.
Raj: Try it after PR. If that helps, we can automate a small grid-search for rope_scaling factors during conversion.
Matt: Good plan. Thanks team.
